name: Autosomal Dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Type 2K

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for CMT2K

criteria.description: Presence of a length-dependent sensorimotor neuropathy with distal muscle weakness and atrophy
Electrophysiological evidence of axonal neuropathy with reduced compound muscle action potential amplitudes and normal or mildly reduced conduction velocities
Identification of pathogenic heterozygous mutations in the GDAP1 gene
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected first-degree relatives
Nerve biopsy showing axonal degeneration without significant demyelination

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical neuropathy, electrophysiological evidence of axonal neuropathy, and identification of a pathogenic GDAP1 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis; nerve biopsy is rarely required.

laboratory: Elevated creatine kinase may be mild or absent
imaging: MRI may show muscle atrophy in distal limbs
Nerve ultrasound may show reduced nerve cross-sectional area

distinguishingFeatures: Earlier onset and more severe phenotype
Transient nerve palsies triggered by compression

redFlags: Rapidly progressive weakness or sensory loss
references: Pareyson D, Marchesi C. Diagnosis, natural history, and management of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. Lancet Neurol. 2009;8(7):654-667.
Zimon M, Baets J, Fabrizi GM, et al. Dominant GDAP1 mutations cause predominantly mild CMT phenotypes. Neurology. 2011;77(24):2235-2243.
Orphanet: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2K. ORPHA:99944.
